info.name: TicketWave API
info.description:
Full backend API for TicketWave (local dev instance running on port 8081 — port 8080 is taken by another project on this machine). Swagger UI: http://localhost:8081/swagger-ui.html · OpenAPI JSON: http://localhost:8081/v3/api-docs.

Run the four 'Login as ...' requests in the Auth folder first — each one saves its JWT into a collection variable (customerToken/operatorToken/supportToken/adminToken) that every other request's Authorization header references. All example bodies use every field defined on the request DTO.

The partner flow (folders 15 and 16) is ordered as a chain and must be run top to bottom: create the partner, activate it, issue a credential — whose test script captures the clientId/clientSecret, since the secret is returned exactly once — then exchange those for a token in folder 16 and call /api/partner/routes with it. That token is scoped to /api/partner/** and will not open any customer or admin endpoint.

variable.description: Seeded passenger owned by customer1. Overwritten by 'Create passenger' response.
Seeded INITIATED booking owned by customer1. Overwritten by 'Create booking' response.
Seeded CONFIRMED+paid booking owned by customer1 — used for the refund example.
Filled by 'Create user (admin)'. Update-role example targets this, never a real seeded account.
Only needed for 'Confirm a 3DS challenge' — take it from a payment left in PENDING_3DS.
Filled by 'Issue API credential' — returned by the API exactly once and never readable again.
Filled by 'Get partner token'. Scoped to /api/partner/** only.

request.description: Public. Always creates a CUSTOMER account — role can't be chosen here. Re-running with the same username/email returns 409.
Saves the token into {{customerToken}}. Seeded customers: customer1..customer30, all with password SeedPass123!
Saves the token into {{operatorToken}}. Seeded operators: operator1..operator6.
Saves the token into {{supportToken}}. Seeded support agents: support1..support3.
Saves the token into {{adminToken}}. Seeded admins: admin1, admin2.

query.description: Events only — leave blank for travel routes

request.description: Every filter is optional and composable. No auth required.

header.description: Optional — include to see heldByMe correctly for your own holds. Omit entirely for pure guest browsing.

request.description: Returns every seat (AVAILABLE/HELD/BOOKED) with a real computed estimatedFare per seat.
No body. Reserves the seat for the configured TTL (default 10 min). Re-calling refreshes/extends your own hold; 409 if someone else holds it or it's booked.
Idempotent no-op if you don't currently hold this seat. Always 204.

Read-only preview, doesn't consume a redemption. NOTE: no promo codes are seeded in this dev DB by default, so this returns 404 PROMO_CODE_NOT_FOUND unless you've inserted one — that's expected, not a bug.
idType is free text in practice: passport | national_id | driver_license. Saves the new id into {{passengerId}} so Update/Delete below target it instead of a real seeded passenger.
Run 'Create passenger' first so {{passengerId}} points at a passenger you actually own (404 otherwise, on someone else's id).
Deletes {{passengerId}} — run 'Create passenger' first if you don't want to delete a real seeded passenger.
Holds every listed seat as part of creation. passengerId must belong to the authenticated caller. promoCode is optional (null or omit). Run 'Hold a seat' first, or just let this hold it fresh.

amount must exactly match the booking's totalAmount (check via 'Get booking' first). reference is the idempotency key — {{$randomUUID}} auto-generates a fresh one each send so re-running doesn't collide with the unique constraint on payments.reference. method: card | paypal | wallet (free text).
Only works while the booking is still INITIATED (unpaid). 409 if already CONFIRMED/CANCELLED.
No body. Targets {{paidBookingId}} (a seeded CONFIRMED+paid booking) rather than {{bookingId}}, since only a paid booking can be refunded. Applies the cancellation policy and cancels the booking.
EN25TW is customer1's seeded CONFIRMED booking's PNR. Support/admin only.
INITIATED -> CONFIRMED without a payment. 'Record payment' below already confirms as a side effect, so this is the path for a booking settled outside the API.
Only for a payment left in PENDING_3DS. Use card 4000000000003220 on 'Record payment' to produce one, then send its id here as {{paymentId}}.
Every booking owned by the calling customer.

query.description: Repeat the parameter for multiple seats.

request.description: Read-only. Returns the fare difference and whether payment is required, without changing anything — call this before the reschedule below.
Read-only. Shows which policy applies (FULL_REFUND / PARTIAL_REFUND / none) and the refundable amount. Returns eligible=false near departure instead of failing.

query.description: Matches PNR, username or email. Blank/absent returns an empty list rather than everything.
Passenger surname on the booking — the second factor that makes this safe to expose unauthenticated.

request.description: No token. PNR alone is guessable, so the surname must match.
decision: APPROVE | REJECT. Only works on a PENDING refund — 409 otherwise. {{refundId}} defaults to a seeded pending refund; each one can only be settled once.
This really changes customer1's email in the dev DB. Harmless to re-run (409 only if the new address collides with someone else's).

WARNING: this really changes customer1's real login password to NewSeedPass123! — every other request in this collection that logs in as customer1 with SeedPass123! will start failing until you update the 'Login as Customer' body to match. Prefer running this against the 'postman_customer' account from Register instead.
Auto-creates a default row (USD, no seat preference, notifications on) on first call for any account seeded before this feature existed.
seatPreference: WINDOW | AISLE | null (no preference). preferredCurrency must be a 3-letter ISO code.
16 is customer1's seeded user id.
The only way to provision OPERATOR/SUPPORT/ADMIN accounts — self-registration always creates CUSTOMER. role: CUSTOMER | OPERATOR | SUPPORT | ADMIN. Saves the new id into {{createdUserId}}.
Targets {{createdUserId}} (from 'Create user' above) rather than a real seeded account. Run 'Create user (admin-provisioned)' first.
type: FLIGHT | BUS | TRAIN | EVENT. For EVENT routes, set venue and leave origin/destination null; for travel routes, the reverse. Owned by the authenticated operator.
routeId (1) must be owned by operator1 — it is, in the seed data. status is optional (defaults to SCHEDULED); shown here for completeness. status: SCHEDULED | DELAYED | CANCELLED | COMPLETED.
status is optional (defaults to AVAILABLE). seatNumber must be unique within the schedule. status: AVAILABLE | HELD | BOOKED.
Only status and priceModifier are mutable after creation — schedule/seatNumber/class are structural. {{seatId}} (6) must belong to a schedule owned by operator1.
Route 1 belongs to operator1 in the seed data. A route owned by someone else returns 404, not 403 — foreign resources are invisible rather than forbidden.
routeId is ignored on update — a schedule cannot be moved to another route. Setting status CANCELLED is how a trip is called off.
Assignable to a schedule via ScheduleRequest.driverId. Overlapping assignments are rejected with 409.
For an operator belonging to a partner, this lists the whole partner's fleet, not just its own drivers.
type: FLIGHT | BUS | TRAIN | EVENT. Assignable via ScheduleRequest.vehicleId; overlapping assignments are rejected with 409.
Most recent first: account creation, role changes, refund decisions, etc.

query.description: Substring match on the acting username.

request.description: Every filter is optional; delete the ones you do not want. All-empty matches everything.
surchargeRate is a multiplier delta applied on top of the seat's own price modifier: 0.25 means +25%. Range -1.0 to 5.0; negative is a discount.
A JSON array. All-or-nothing: one invalid entry rejects the whole batch.
discountType: PERCENTAGE | FIXED_AMOUNT. validTo must be in the future. code is unique — re-running returns 409. maxRedemptions is optional (null = unlimited).
Deactivating is the way to retire a code — they are never deleted, so past bookings keep a valid reference. Recorded in the audit log.
Occupancy and revenue across the calling operator's own schedules only — scoped by the authenticated principal, not by a parameter.
Aggregates the append-only ledger over [from, to): payments in, refunds out, net. Both parameters are required.
Created in PENDING status. commissionRate is 0..1. Saves the new id into {{partnerId}}.
status: PENDING | ACTIVE | SUSPENDED. Run this before issuing a credential — a token request for a non-ACTIVE partner is rejected.

No body. The clientSecret is returned ONLY here — it is BCrypt-hashed at rest and can never be read back. The test script captures it into {{partnerClientSecret}}; lose it and you must issue a new credential.
Shows clientId, status and lastUsedAt — never the secret.
Note the path is not nested under the partner — credential ids are globally unique. Already-issued tokens stay valid until they expire; revocation only stops new ones.

Returns a signing secret, shown only once. Deliveries carry X-TicketWave-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body>. To see one fire, approve a refund on a booking whose route belongs to this partner's operator.
status: ACTIVE | DISABLED. Like credentials, the path is not nested under the partner.

Client-credentials exchange — no user is involved. Run 'Issue API credential' first; its test script fills both variables used here. Rejected if the credential is revoked or the partner is not ACTIVE. Saves the token into {{partnerToken}}.

Returns only routes whose operator belongs to this partner. A brand-new partner has no operators yet, so an empty array here is correct, not a failure — attach an operator account to the partner to see data. Note this token does NOT work on /api/routes or any customer endpoint.
